content.thinking:
Since the caller isn't authorised, I shouldn't disclose anything, but I can offer to pass along a message, explain the consent process, or arrange a third-party payment with an address. I should also plan to email the tenant (my preferred contact method) to flag who called and seek consent, noting the tenant seems vulnerable and "very down" — this might warrant a gentle wellbeing check or mentioning Samaritans, though escalation should stay measured given the mild nature of the concern.

I'll log the call with details shared and send a wellbeing-conscious email to the tenant, since the caller has no contact on file and I can't message back except through logging. No tickets needed here, just these two actions.

arguments.party_name: Grace (caller, says she is Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller claims to be tenant's mum and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile. CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Caller gave address and a DOB (2 Nov, no year) - not authority. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payments, contact details, not even confirming the tenancy details). Told her: we can pass a message to Jonah; Jonah can give written consent or add her as an authorised contact; if she wants to pay, a third party can pay towards rent quoting the property address, without being told the balance. Offered Samaritans 116 123 if she is worried about his wellbeing. Tenant to be told of the call by email.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she wants to help with your rent. We told her nothing about your account or contact details, because we have no consent from you on file. She can pay towards rent by quoting the property address, without us sharing any balance. If you are happy for us to talk to her, or want to add her as an authorised contact, just reply to this email and we will set it up. If you'd rather we didn't, no need to do anything. If things feel hard at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123, and you can reply here any time. Thanks, Mare and Co Lettings

Since the caller isn't authorised, I shouldn't disclose anything, but I can offer to pass along a message, explain the consent process, or arrange a third-party payment with an address. I should also plan to email the tenant (my preferred contact method) to flag who called and seek consent, noting the tenant seems vulnerable and "very down" — this might warrant a gentle wellbeing check or mentioning Samaritans, though escalation should stay measured given the mild nature of the concern.

I'll log the call with details shared and send a wellbeing-conscious email to the tenant, since the caller has no contact on file and I can't message back except through logging. No tickets needed here, just these two actions.

arguments.party_name: Grace (caller, says she is Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller claims to be tenant's mum and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile. CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Caller gave address and a DOB (2 Nov, no year) - not authority. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payments, contact details, not even confirming the tenancy details). Told her: we can pass a message to Jonah; Jonah can give written consent or add her as an authorised contact; if she wants to pay, a third party can pay towards rent quoting the property address, without being told the balance. Offered Samaritans 116 123 if she is worried about his wellbeing. Tenant to be told of the call by email.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she wants to help with your rent. We told her nothing about your account or contact details, because we have no consent from you on file. She can pay towards rent by quoting the property address, without us sharing any balance. If you are happy for us to talk to her, or want to add her as an authorised contact, just reply to this email and we will set it up. If you'd rather we didn't, no need to do anything. If things feel hard at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123, and you can reply here any time. Thanks, Mare and Co Lettings
